key_insight: Large language models can extract semantic concepts from materials-science abstracts to build temporal concept graphs, and a trained predictor can forecast which novel concept combinations are likely to emerge—helping experts discover promising new research directions.
problem_solved: Literature grows too fast for manual curation; it is hard to anticipate novel, interdisciplinary topic combinations from historical publication data and surface useful, actionable suggestions for researchers.
method: Use LLMs to extract and normalize concepts and relations from materials-science abstracts to create a semantic representation.
Construct temporal concept graphs that capture co-occurrence and evolution of concepts over time.
Train a predictive model on historical graph dynamics to forecast emerging concept combinations and present ranked suggestions for expert review.
impact: Provides a scalable, data-driven way to forecast research trends and augment human creativity—useful for ML-driven literature analysis, research prioritization, and building researcher-in-the-loop discovery tools.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: abstracts → LLM extraction → concept normalization → temporal concept graph → predictor → expert suggestions
Animated or small-multiples concept-graph showing node/edge growth and newly emerging links over time
Heatmap or ranked bar chart comparing predicted emerging topic combinations with retrospective ground truth (precision/recall)
Iconic workflow showing expert-in-the-loop validation and suggestion adoption
paper_title: Predicting new research directions in materials science using large language models and concept graphs
paper_authors: Thomas Marwitz, Alexander Colsmann, Ben Breitung, Christoph Brabec, Christoph Kirchlechner
